intro: Not a protocol on the wire, but the rulebook for securing a plant's control systems (OT). It splits a plant into zones, groups of devices that need the same protection, and lets them talk only through conduits with clear rules. Each zone gets a target security level, and seven foundational requirements say what that level means.

inside.title: Zones and conduits
inside.text: The solar plant has four zones: the office, a DMZ, control and field. They talk only through conduits, here guarded by two firewalls. SCADA polling an inverter crosses FW-2, and a rule allows exactly that.

historian.title: Into the DMZ
historian.text: The historian in the DMZ collects the plant's values from SCADA. The DMZ is the buffer: the office and the plant never talk directly.

office.title: The office reads the DMZ
office.text: An engineer in the office opens today's production report. It comes from the historian; the office never reaches the plant.

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.text: A laptop in the office tries to reach an inverter directly. No rule allows it, so FW-1 drops the connection and logs it.

vendor.title: Vendor access
vendor.text: The inverter's maker must update INV-07. Its engineer logs in to the jump host with two factors and works from there, during an approved job. Everything is logged.

frames.historian-read: Give me the latest plant values
frames.blocked: Connect me to inverter INV-07, port 502
frames.vendor-login: Vendor login: password and one-time code

notes.scada-poll: Modbus TCP from SCADA in the control zone to the inverter in the field zone. The connection crosses FW-2, and conduit C3 has a rule for exactly this: from SCADA, to the inverters, TCP 502.
notes.historian-read: Conduit C2 lets the historian, and only the historian, open OPC UA (TCP 4840) to SCADA. The historian keeps a copy of the plant's data in the DMZ.
notes.scada-values: The answer needs no rule of its own: the firewall knows it belongs to a connection it allowed.
notes.office-read: Office users read the historian in the DMZ, never the plant. If the office is attacked, the attacker finds a copy of the data, not the controls.
notes.blocked: No rule lets the office reach the field zone, so the last rule of C1 drops it. The laptop gets no answer. The log entry is worth an alarm: the laptop may be infected, or someone is trying.
notes.vendor-login: From the internet, the vendor reaches the jump host in the DMZ and nothing else. The jump host asks for a password and a one-time code from the engineer's phone: two factors, so a stolen password is not enough. It records the session.
notes.vendor-session: From the jump host, conduit C4 allows HTTPS to the inverters, only while the job is approved. The vendor's own laptop never touches the plant network.

sl1.name: Mistakes
sl1.note: Protects against error and chance: someone plugs in the wrong cable or opens the wrong file.

sl2.name: Simple attacks
sl2.note: Against someone who means it, with simple means: common tools, general IT skills, little money.

sl3.name: Skilled attacks
sl3.note: Against an attacker who knows OT systems, with good tools and some money.

sl4.name: Well-funded attacks
sl4.note: Against a team with deep OT skills, much money and much time, such as a state.

fr1.name: FR 1 · Identification and authentication
fr1.note: Know who is asking, a person, a program or a device, before letting them in.

fr2.name: FR 2 · Use control
fr2.note: Once known, each may do only what their role allows. An operator may not load new firmware.

fr3.name: FR 3 · System integrity
fr3.note: Software, settings and messages cannot be changed without it being noticed.

fr4.name: FR 4 · Data confidentiality
fr4.note: Keep secrets secret, stored or on the wire: passwords, keys, some data. Only 2 here: most plant values are not secret.

fr5.name: FR 5 · Restricted data flow
fr5.note: Data flows only where it must: the zones, the conduits and their rules.

fr6.name: FR 6 · Timely response to events
fr6.note: Logs and alarms, so that an attack is seen and handled in time.

fr7.name: FR 7 · Resource availability
fr7.note: The plant keeps running under load or attack, and can be restored from backups.

facts.standard: ISA/IEC 62443 series: zones and conduits in 62443-3-2, system requirements in 62443-3-3
facts.between: Asset owner, system integrator and product supplier: each has its own parts
facts.transport: None of its own: its rules cover every protocol in the plant
facts.security: A target security level, SL 1 to SL 4, for each zone

tips: A rule from any to any, even for one day, joins two zones into one. Name the source, the destination and the port.
Let remote access end in the DMZ. A vendor VPN straight into the control zone skips every conduit.
Shared accounts break FR 1: nobody can tell who did what. Give every person their own login, vendors too.
Three levels are often mixed up: SL-T is the zone's target, SL-C what a product can reach, SL-A what the built zone really reaches. Check SL-A, not the datasheet.

anatomy.levels: Security levels: who a zone must stand up to
anatomy.vector: The target of the control zone: one level for each foundational requirement

playground.file: The plant's zones and the rules of its conduits. Find the rule behind each step.
playground.zones: A zone is a group of devices that need the same protection. SL-T is the security level the zone must reach.
playground.enterprise: SL 1: the office network. It is IT, not OT, and the plant treats it as untrusted.
playground.dmz: SL 2: the buffer between office and plant. Connections end here, and new ones start here.
playground.control: SL 3: SCADA runs the plant, so it must stand up to a skilled attacker who knows OT.
playground.field: SL 3 as well: the inverters and the RTU act on the grid.
playground.conduits: A conduit groups the connections between two zones. Each rule names a source, a destination and a service; the first rule that matches decides.
playground.office: The office reads the plant's data from the historian, never from the plant.
playground.vendor: From the internet, only the jump host is reachable. The jump host asks for two factors.
playground.deny: Everything else is dropped and logged. This rule stops the laptop in step 4.
playground.historian: One source, one destination, one port: OPC UA from the historian to SCADA.
playground.scada-poll: SCADA reads the inverters with Modbus TCP: step 1.
playground.job: Vendor sessions reach the inverters only while a job is approved. The rest of the time, this rule is off.
